questions.question: On a number line, which number is the biggest?
questions.explain: Look at the hundreds digit first. Seven is the biggest hundreds digit, so 734 is the biggest number. The ones digit does not decide which number is biggest.

questions.question: On a number line, which number is the smallest?
questions.explain: Start with the hundreds digit. Two is the smallest hundreds digit, so 263 is the smallest. Picking a number just because its ones digit is small is a common trap.

questions.question: Is 456 bigger than 465?
questions.explain: The hundreds digits match, so look at the tens digit. Six is more than five, so 465 is bigger. The ones digit does not matter here.

questions.question: On a number line, where does 508 sit?
questions.explain: 508 has 5 hundreds and 0 tens, so it sits just past 500, before 510. Looking at only the ones digit can trick you into the wrong spot.

questions.question: Lily has 234 stickers. Tom has 243 stickers. Who has more?
options: You cannot tell from the numbers
questions.explain: The hundreds digits match, so look at the tens digit. Tom has 4 tens and Lily has 3, so Tom has more. The ones digit (4 vs 3) does not decide it.

questions.question: Anna jumps 152 times. Ben jumps 125 times. Cara jumps 251 times. Who jumped the most?
questions.explain: Look at the hundreds digit first. Two is bigger than one, so Cara jumped the most. Ben has the biggest ones digit, but that does not make his number the biggest.

questions.question: You want to find the biggest number from 372, 327, 732, and 273. What do you look at first?
questions.explain: Always start with the hundreds digit. Seven is the biggest hundreds digit, so 732 wins. Looking at the ones or tens digit first can give you the wrong answer.

questions.question: Sam writes four numbers on cards: 608, 680, 806, 860. Which card has the biggest number?
questions.explain: The hundreds digit decides first: 8 beats 6. Then the tens digit: 6 beats 0. So 860 is the biggest. Picking 608 just because its ones digit is 8 is a common trap.

questions.question: Mia has 453 marbles. Her friend has 435 marbles. Who has more, and why?
options: Mia, the tens digit is bigger
Friend, the ones digit is bigger
Friend, the hundreds digit is bigger
questions.explain: The hundreds digits match, so look at the tens digit. Mia has 5 tens and her friend has 3, so Mia has more. Comparing the ones digits (3 vs 5) gives the wrong answer.

questions.question: Put these from smallest to biggest: 234, 342, 423
questions.explain: Start with the hundreds digit: 2, then 3, then 4. That gives 234, 342, 423. Going from biggest to smallest is a common mix-up when a question asks for smallest to biggest.

questions.question: A number is bigger than 384 and smaller than 392. Which could it be?
questions.explain: 388 sits between 384 and 392. Check the tens digit first: it must be 8 or 9. Then check the ones digit to see if it fits. 395 is too big; 376 and 382 are too small.

questions.question: Max says: 624 is bigger than 642 because 4 is more than 2. What did Max get wrong?
options: He added the digits instead of comparing
He put the tens digit in the ones place
He mixed up the order of the digits
He used the ones digit, not the tens
questions.explain: Max looked at the ones digits (4 and 2), but the tens digits (2 and 4) are what matter. Since 4 tens is more than 2 tens, 642 is actually the bigger number.
